messages:
devon: Quick idea — what if we show a tiny privilege badge cluster on each route row (read/write/exec) and a micro-sparkline for recent deny vs allow rate?

jess: ooh I like that. compact + signals. are we thinking hover-to-expand for details? :thinking_face:

maria: hover makes sense for desktop. on mobile it should open a panel. also need to surface 'why denied' (entitlement vs quota vs routing policy).

sam: big question: where do we compute effective permissions? client-side merging of role blobs or a single /authz/eval endpoint?

devon: leaning toward server eval — one canonical source, avoids client mismatches. but perf concern for large tenant lists.

infra-bot: deploy-check: authz service QPS currently 120/s, p95 latency 38ms. adding eval calls per route view could spike that.

jess: could we cache eval per user+tenant for 60s and invalidate on role change events?

maria: +1 but we need telemetry to know cache hit/miss. propose events: permission_preview.view, permission_preview.cache_hit, permission_preview.miss, permission_preview.source(quota|routing|role).

sam: also need to show quota impact inline. like a tiny counter: "quota: 85% used" when relevant. UX: red badge when route access is blocked by quota.

devon: UX mocks: compact badges (3px icons), sparkline 7px high with green/amber/red segments, click -> full modal with policy tree and simulated request example.

jess: another internal API debate — should the modal fetch the policy tree via /policies/:route or reuse the same /authz/eval response? fewer calls if eval contains reasons.

maria: prefer eval to include an array of blame reasons (e.g., ["quota_limit", "role_missing:call_write"]). helps the modal render human text without extra calls.

sam: downside: larger payloads for the list view. maybe we return short reason tags in list call and expand reasons in modal with a separate eval?

devon: tradeoff. performance vs consistency. propose hybrid: list call gets summaries + sparkline + small reason tag. modal triggers full_eval_if_needed. cache full_eval for 2m.

jess: rollout UX — feature flag so customers can opt-in to the new badges. default off for enterprise tenants until we finish privacy review.

maria: privacy note: telemetry must hash principal IDs; don't send raw service-account names to metrics. include K-anonymity check for low-volume tenants.

infra-bot: note: will need a schema change in authz responses: add fields ["summary_tags","sparkline_counts","expanded_reason_id"] (proposal in RFC-742).

sam: for quota and routing policy interplay: when routing fallback happens we should show the route actually used and why (e.g., routed to cheaper model because tier exhausted). badge should reflect effective route permission, not just canonical.

devon: implementation TODOs: 1) API: authz summary endpoint prototype, 2) client: badge component + hover modal, 3) telemetry: events + schema, 4) rollout flag + admin toggle, 5) privacy review and docs.

jess: can someone pick up a quick spike? 1 day to mock server payloads and perf sim?

maria: I'll take the spike. will post mock payloads in #eng-platform tomorrow.

sam: i'll write the client badge and make it toggle behind feature flag.

devon: thanks! tagging product-bot to capture the feature ask for roadmap.

product-bot: Added ticket INFR-1218 "Privilege badges + sparklines in route list" to backlog, priority: P2, owner: TBD.

maria: one more: add acceptance criteria — "hover shows top 3 reasons; modal shows full policy tree; telemetry emitted on view and expand; cache TTL 60s default".

jess: agreed. will add to the ticket. :thumbsup:

devon: cool. we'll reconvene after the spike and perf numbers. thanks all."
